entries.need: Identify and describe a catalog.
entries.label: catalog
entries.definition: A curated collection of metadata about resources (e.g., datasets and data services in the context of a data catalog)
usage_notes: A Web-based data catalog is typically represented as a single instance of this class.

entries.need: Find the other catalogs whose contents are of interest in a catalog.
entries.label: catalog
entries.definition: A catalog whose contents are of interest in the context of this catalog.
entries.need_draft: Find the catalog of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Preserve interest in another catalog; do not equate this with a part-of relationship. Basis: pinned definition.

entries.need: Find the contact point of a catalog.
entries.label: contact point
entries.definition: Relevant contact information for the cataloged resource. Use of vCard is recommended [VCARD-RDF].

entries.need: Find the datasets listed in a catalog.
entries.label: dataset
entries.definition: A collection of data that is listed in the catalog.
entries.need_draft: Find the dataset of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition.

entries.need: Find the available distributions of a catalog.
entries.label: dataset distribution
entries.definition: An available distribution of the dataset.
entries.need_draft: Find the dataset distribution of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition.

entries.need: Find the keywords or tags describing a catalog.
entries.label: keyword/tag
entries.definition: A keyword or tag describing the resource.
entries.need_draft: Find the keyword/tag of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition.

entries.need: Find the landing page of a catalog.
entries.label: landing page
entries.definition: A Web page that can be navigated to in a Web browser to gain access to the catalog, a dataset, its distributions and/or additional information.
usage_notes: If the distribution(s) are accessible only through a landing page (i.e. direct download URLs are not known), then the landing page link SHOULD be duplicated as dcat:accessURL on a distribution. (see § 5.7 Dataset available only behind some Web page)

entries.need: Find descriptions of the relationships between a catalog and other resources.
entries.label: qualified relation
entries.definition: Link to a description of a relationship with another resource
usage_notes: Used to link to another resource where the nature of the relationship is known but does not match one of the standard [DCTERMS] properties (dct:hasPart, dct:isPartOf, dct:conformsTo, dct:isFormatOf, dct:hasFormat, dct:isVersionOf, dct:hasVersion, dct:replaces, dct:isReplacedBy, dct:references, dct:isReferencedBy, dct:requires, dct:isRequiredBy) or [PROV-O] properties (prov:wasDerivedFrom, prov:wasInfluencedBy, prov:wasQuotedFrom, prov:wasRevisionOf, prov:hadPrimarySource, prov:alternateOf, prov:specializationOf).
entries.need_draft: Find the qualified relation of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the records describing resources listed in a catalog.
entries.label: catalog record
entries.definition: A record describing the registration of a single dataset or data service that is part of the catalog.
entries.need_draft: Find the catalog record of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition.

entries.need: Find the data services listed in a catalog.
entries.label: service
entries.definition: A site or end-point that is listed in the catalog.
entries.need_draft: Find the service of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition.

entries.need: Find the minimum spatial separation resolvable in a catalog, measured in meters.
entries.label: spatial resolution in meters
entries.definition: Minimum spatial separation resolvable in a dataset, measured in meters.
usage_notes: If the dataset is an image or grid this should correspond to the spacing of items. For other kinds of spatial datasets, this property will usually indicate the smallest distance between items in the dataset.
entries.need_draft: Find the spatial resolution in meters of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Preserve resolvable separation and meters, distinct from geographic coverage. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the minimum time interval resolvable in a catalog.
entries.label: temporal resolution
entries.definition: Minimum time period resolvable in the dataset.
usage_notes: If the dataset is a time-series this should correspond to the spacing of items in the series. For other kinds of dataset, this property will usually indicate the smallest time difference between items in the dataset.
entries.need_draft: Find the temporal resolution of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Preserve resolvable interval, distinct from temporal coverage. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the subject categories of a catalog.
entries.label: theme/category
entries.definition: A main category of the resource. A resource can have multiple themes.
usage_notes: The set of skos:Concepts used to categorize the resources are organized in a skos:ConceptScheme describing all the categories and their relations in the catalog.
entries.need_draft: Find the theme/category of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the classification scheme used by a catalog.
entries.label: themes
entries.definition: A knowledge organization system (KOS) used to classify catalog's datasets and services.
usage_notes: It is recommended that the taxonomy is organized in a skos:ConceptScheme, skos:Collection, owl:Ontology or similar, which allows each member to be denoted by an IRI and published as Linked Data.
entries.need_draft: Find the themes of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. The classification scheme is distinct from the categories assigned to a resource. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the access restrictions of a catalog.
entries.label: access restrictions
entries.definition: Information about who can access the resource or an indication of its security status.
usage_notes: Information about licenses and rights MAY be provided for the Resource. See also guidance at § 8. License and rights statements.

entries.need: Find how often a catalog is published or updated.
entries.label: frequency
entries.definition: The frequency at which dataset is published.
usage_notes: The value of dct:accrualPeriodicity gives the rate at which the dataset-as-a-whole is updated. This may be complemented by dcat:temporalResolution to give the time between collected data points in a time series.
entries.need_draft: Find the frequency of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the standard or specification that a catalog conforms to.
entries.label: conformance
entries.definition: An established standard to which the described resource conforms.
usage_notes: This property SHOULD be used to indicate the model, schema, ontology, view or profile that the cataloged resource content conforms to.
entries.need_draft: Find the conformance of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the resource creator of a catalog.
entries.label: resource creator
entries.definition: The entity responsible for producing the resource.
usage_notes: Resources of type foaf:Agent are recommended as values for this property.

entries.need: Find the description of a catalog.
entries.label: description
entries.definition: A free-text account of the item.

entries.need: Find the resources listed as members of a catalog.
entries.label: has part
entries.definition: An item that is listed in the catalog.
usage_notes: This is the most general predicate for membership of a catalog. Use of a more specific sub-property is recommended when available.
entries.need_draft: Find the has part of a catalog.

entries.need: Find the identifier of a catalog.
entries.label: identifier
entries.definition: A unique identifier of the item.
usage_notes: The identifier might be used as part of the URI of the item, but still having it represented explicitly is useful.

entries.need: Find the resources that refer to a catalog.
entries.label: is referenced by
entries.definition: A related resource, such as a publication, that references, cites, or otherwise points to the cataloged resource.
usage_notes: This property is used to associate a resource with the resource (of type dcat:Resource) in question. For other relations to resources not covered with this property, the more generic property dcat:qualifiedRelation can be used. See also § 13. Qualified relations.
entries.need_draft: Find the is referenced by of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the date when a catalog was formally issued or published.
entries.label: issued
entries.definition: Date of formal issuance (e.g., publication) of the item.
usage_notes: This property SHOULD be set using the first known date of issuance.
entries.need_draft: Find the issued of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the languages used in the textual metadata of a catalog.
entries.label: language
entries.definition: A language of the item. This refers to the natural language used for textual metadata (i.e. titles, descriptions, etc) of a cataloged resource (i.e. dataset or service) or the textual values of a dataset distribution
usage_notes: If representations of a dataset are available for each language separately, define an instance of dcat:Distribution for each language and describe the specific language of each distribution using dct:language (i.e. the dataset will have multiple dct:language values and each distribution will have just one as the value of its dct:language property).
entries.need_draft: Find the language of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Metadata language must not be confused with the language of the data values. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the licence of a catalog.
entries.label: licence
entries.definition: A legal document under which the resource is made available.
usage_notes: Information about licenses and rights MAY be provided for the Resource. See also guidance at § 8. License and rights statements.

entries.need: Find the most recent date when a catalog was changed or modified.
entries.label: last modified
entries.definition: Most recent date on which the item was changed, updated or modified.
usage_notes: The value of this property indicates a change to the actual item, not a change to the catalog record. An absent value MAY indicate that the item has never changed after its initial publication, or that the date of last modification is not known, or that the item is continuously updated.
entries.need_draft: Find the last modified of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Preserve the subject of modification; a record date is not the underlying dataset date. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the publisher of a catalog.
entries.label: publisher
entries.definition: The entity responsible for making the item available.
usage_notes: Resources of type foaf:Agent are recommended as values for this property.

entries.need: Find the resources related to a catalog.
entries.label: relation
entries.definition: A resource with an unspecified relationship to the cataloged item.
usage_notes: dct:relation SHOULD be used where the nature of the relationship between a cataloged item and related resources is not known. A more specific sub-property SHOULD be used if the nature of the relationship of the link is known. The property dcat:distribution SHOULD be used to link from a dcat:Dataset to a representation of the dataset, described as a dcat:Distribution
entries.need_draft: Find the relation of a catalog.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the rights of a catalog.
entries.label: rights
entries.definition: A statement that concerns all rights not addressed with dct:license or dct:accessRights, such as copyright statements.
usage_notes: Information about licenses and rights MAY be provided for the Resource. See also guidance at § 8. License and rights statements.

entries.need: Find the geographic area covered by a catalog.
entries.label: spatial/geographical coverage
entries.definition: The geographical area covered by the dataset.
usage_notes: The spatial coverage of a dataset may be encoded as an instance of dct:Location, or may be indicated using a URI reference (link) to a resource describing a location. It is recommended that links are to entries in a well maintained gazetteer such as Geonames.

entries.need: Find the time period covered by a catalog.

entries.need_draft: Find the temporal coverage of a catalog.

entries.need: Find the title of a catalog.

entries.definition: A name given to the item.

entries.need: Find the type/genre of a catalog.
entries.label: type/genre
entries.definition: The nature or genre of the resource.

entries.need: Find the homepage of a catalog.
entries.label: homepage
entries.definition: A homepage of the catalog (a public Web document usually available in HTML).
usage_notes: foaf:homepage is an inverse functional property (IFP) which means that it MUST be unique and precisely identify the Web-page for the resource. This property indicates the canonical Web-page, which might be helpful in cases where there is more than one Web-page about the resource.

entries.need: Find the machine-readable policy expressing the rights associated with a catalog.
entries.label: has policy
entries.definition: An ODRL conformant policy expressing the rights associated with the resource.
usage_notes: Information about rights expressed as an ODRL policy [ODRL-MODEL] using the ODRL vocabulary [ODRL-VOCAB] MAY be provided for the resource. See also guidance at § 8. License and rights statements.
entries.need_draft: Find the has policy of a catalog.

entries.need: Find the agents with responsibility for a catalog and their roles.
entries.label: qualified attribution
entries.definition: Link to an Agent having some form of responsibility for the resource
usage_notes: Used to link to an Agent where the nature of the relationship is known but does not match one of the standard [DCTERMS] properties (dct:creator, dct:publisher). Use dcat:hadRole on the prov:Attribution to capture the responsibility of the Agent with respect to the Resource. See § 13.1 Relationships between datasets and agents for usage examples.

entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Preserve responsibility and the role described by qualified attribution. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the activity that generated or provides the business context for creating a catalog.
entries.label: was generated by
entries.definition: An activity that generated, or provides the business context for, the creation of the dataset.
usage_notes: Use prov:qualifiedGeneration to attach additional details about the relationship between the dataset and the activity, e.g. the exact time that the dataset was produced during the lifetime of a project

entries.need: Identify and describe a catalog record.
entries.label: catalog record
entries.definition: A record in a catalog, describing the registration of a single dcat:Resource.
usage_notes: This class is optional and not all catalogs will use it. It exists for catalogs where a distinction is made between metadata about a dataset or service and metadata about the entry in the catalog about the dataset or service. For example, the publication date property of the dataset reflects the date when the information was originally made available by the publishing agency, while the publication date of the catalog record is the date when the dataset was added to the catalog. In cases where both dates differ, or where only the latter is known, the publication date SHOULD only be specified for the catalog record. Notice that the W3C PROV Ontology [PROV-O] allows describing further provenance information such as the details of the process and the agent involved in a particular change to a dataset or its registration.

entries.need: Identify and describe a distribution.
entries.label: distribution
entries.definition: A specific representation of a dataset. A dataset might be available in multiple serializations that may differ in various ways, including natural language, media-type or format, schematic organization, temporal and spatial resolution, level of detail or profiles (which might specify any or all of the above).
usage_notes: This represents a general availability of a dataset. It implies no information about the actual access method of the data, i.e. whether by direct download, API, or through a Web page. The use of dcat:downloadURL property indicates directly downloadable distributions.

usage_notes: dcat:accessURL SHOULD be used for the URL of a service or location that can provide access to this distribution, typically through a Web form, query or API call. dcat:downloadURL is preferred for direct links to downloadable resources. entries.definition: Information about who can access the resource or an indication of its security status.
usage_notes: Information about licenses and rights MAY be provided for the Resource. See also guidance at § 8. License and rights statements.

entries.need: Find the standard or specification that a resource conforms to.
entries.label: conforms to
entries.definition: An established standard to which the described resource conforms.
usage_notes: This property SHOULD be used to indicate the model, schema, ontology, view or profile that the cataloged resource content conforms to.
entries.need_draft: Find the conforms to of a resource.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the resource creator of a resource.
entries.label: resource creator
entries.definition: The entity responsible for producing the resource.
usage_notes: Resources of type foaf:Agent are recommended as values for this property.

entries.need: Find the description of a resource.
entries.label: description
entries.definition: A free-text account of the item.

entries.need: Find the identifier of a resource.
entries.label: identifier
entries.definition: A unique identifier of the item.
usage_notes: The identifier might be used as part of the URI of the item, but still having it represented explicitly is useful.

entries.need: Find the resources that refer to a resource.
entries.label: is referenced by
entries.definition: A related resource, such as a publication, that references, cites, or otherwise points to the cataloged resource.
usage_notes: This property is used to associate a resource with the resource (of type dcat:Resource) in question. For other relations to resources not covered with this property, the more generic property dcat:qualifiedRelation can be used. See also § 13. Qualified relations.
entries.need_draft: Find the is referenced by of a resource.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the date when a resource was formally issued or published.
entries.label: release date
entries.definition: Date of formal issuance (e.g., publication) of the item.
usage_notes: This property SHOULD be set using the first known date of issuance.
entries.need_draft: Find the release date of a resource.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the language of a resource.
entries.label: language
entries.definition: A language of the item. This refers to the natural language used for textual metadata (i.e. titles, descriptions, etc) of a cataloged resource (i.e. dataset or service) or the textual values of a dataset distribution
usage_notes: If representations of a dataset are available for each language separately, define an instance of dcat:Distribution for each language and describe the specific language of each distribution using dct:language (i.e. the dataset will have multiple dct:language values and each distribution will have just one as the value of its dct:language property).

entries.need: Find the license of a resource.
entries.label: license
entries.definition: A legal document under which the resource is made available.
usage_notes: Information about licenses and rights MAY be provided for the Resource. See also guidance at § 8. License and rights statements.

entries.need: Find the most recent date when a resource was changed or modified.
entries.label: update/modification date
entries.definition: Most recent date on which the item was changed, updated or modified.
usage_notes: The value of this property indicates a change to the actual item, not a change to the catalog record. An absent value MAY indicate that the item has never changed after its initial publication, or that the date of last modification is not known, or that the item is continuously updated.
entries.need_draft: Find the update/modification date of a resource.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Preserve the subject of modification; a record date is not the underlying dataset date. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the publisher of a resource.
entries.label: publisher
entries.definition: The entity responsible for making the item available.
usage_notes: Resources of type foaf:Agent are recommended as values for this property.

entries.need: Find the resources related to a resource.
entries.label: resource relation
entries.definition: A resource with an unspecified relationship to the cataloged item.
usage_notes: dct:relation SHOULD be used where the nature of the relationship between a cataloged item and related resources is not known. A more specific sub-property SHOULD be used if the nature of the relationship of the link is known. The property dcat:distribution SHOULD be used to link from a dcat:Dataset to a representation of the dataset, described as a dcat:Distribution
entries.need_draft: Find the resource relation of a resource.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the rights of a resource.
entries.label: rights
entries.definition: A statement that concerns all rights not addressed with dct:license or dct:accessRights, such as copyright statements.
usage_notes: Information about licenses and rights MAY be provided for the Resource. See also guidance at § 8. License and rights statements.

entries.need: Find the title of a resource.
entries.label: title
entries.definition: A name given to the item.

entries.need: Find the type/genre of a resource.
entries.label: type/genre
entries.definition: The nature or genre of the resource.
usage_notes: To describe the file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource, use the dct:format element.

entries.need: Find the machine-readable policy expressing the rights associated with a resource.
entries.label: has policy
entries.definition: An ODRL conformant policy expressing the rights associated with the resource.
usage_notes: Information about rights expressed as an ODRL policy [ODRL-MODEL] using the ODRL vocabulary [ODRL-VOCAB] MAY be provided for the resource. See also guidance at § 8. License and rights statements.
entries.need_draft: Find the has policy of a resource.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the agents with responsibility for a resource and their roles.
entries.label: qualified attribution
entries.definition: Link to an Agent having some form of responsibility for the resource
usage_notes: Used to link to an Agent where the nature of the relationship is known but does not match one of the standard [DCTERMS] properties (dct:creator, dct:publisher). Use dcat:hadRole on the prov:Attribution to capture the responsibility of the Agent with respect to the Resource. See § 13.1 Relationships between datasets and agents for usage examples.
entries.need_draft: Find the qualified attribution of a resource.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Preserve responsibility and the role described by qualified attribution. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Identify and describe a role.
entries.label: role
entries.definition: A role is the function of a resource or agent with respect to another resource, in the context of resource attribution or resource relationships.
usage_notes: Used in a qualified-relation to specify the role of an Entity with respect to another Entity. It is recommended that the values be managed as a controlled vocabulary of entity roles such as [ISO-19115-1] DS_AssociationTypeCode IANA Registry of Link Relations [IANA-RELATIONS] DataCite metadata schema [DataCite] MARC relators

entries.need: Identify and describe a location.
entries.label: location
entries.definition: A spatial region or named place.
usage_notes: For an extensive geometry (i.e., a set of coordinates denoting the vertices of the relevant geographic area), the property locn:geometry [LOCN] SHOULD be used. For a geographic bounding box delimiting a spatial area the property dcat:bbox SHOULD be used. For the geographic center of a spatial area, or another characteristic point, the property dcat:centroid SHOULD be used.

entries.need: Find the geographic bounding box of a location.
entries.label: bounding box
entries.definition: The geographic bounding box of a resource.
usage_notes: The range of this property is intentionally generic, with the purpose of allowing different geometry encodings. E.g., the geometry could be encoded as WKT (geosparql:asWKT [GeoSPARQL]).
entries.need_draft: Find the bounding box of a location.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Find the centroid of a location.
entries.label: centroid
entries.definition: The geographic center (centroid) of a resource.
usage_notes: The range of this property is intentionally generic, with the purpose of allowing different geometry encodings. E.g., the geometry could be encoded as WKT (geosparql:asWKT [GeoSPARQL]).

entries.need: Find the geometry describing a location.
entries.label: geometry
entries.definition: Associates any resource with the corresponding geometry. [LOCN]
usage_notes: The range of this property is intentionally generic, with the purpose of allowing different geometry encodings. E.g., the geometry could be encoded as WKT (geosparql:asWKT [GeoSPARQL]).
entries.need_draft: Find the geometry of a location.
entries.review_note: AI-assisted review by Codex, 2026-10-19. Clarify the existing property meaning without adding a task, obligation or constraint. Basis: pinned definition and usage notes.

entries.need: Identify and describe a period of time.
entries.label: period of time
entries.definition: An interval of time that is named or defined by its start and end.
usage_notes: The start and end of the interval SHOULD be given by using properties dcat:startDate or time:hasBeginning, and dcat:endDate or time:hasEnd, respectively. The interval can also be open - i.e., it can have just a start or just an end.

entries.need: Find the end date of a period of time.
entries.label: end date
entries.definition: The end of the period.

entries.need: Find the start date of a period of time.
entries.label: start date
entries.definition: The start of the period.

entries.need: Find the beginning of a period of time.
entries.label: beginning
entries.definition: Beginning of a period or interval.
usage_notes: Use of the property time:hasBeginning entails that value of the dct:temporal property is a member of the time:TemporalEntity class from [OWL-TIME]. In this context this could be taken to imply that dct:PeriodOfTime is equivalent to the sub-class time:ProperInterval

entries.need: Find the end of a period of time.
entries.label: end
entries.definition: End of a period or interval.
usage_notes: Use of the property time:hasEnd entails that value of the dct:temporal property is a member of the time:TemporalEntity class from [OWL-TIME]. In this context this could be taken to imply that dct:PeriodOfTime is equivalent to the sub-class time:ProperInterval

entries.need: Identify and describe a concept.
entries.label: concept
entries.definition: A category or a theme used to describe datasets in the catalog.
usage_notes: It is recommended to use either skos:inScheme or skos:topConceptOf on every skos:Concept used to classify datasets to link it to the concept scheme it belongs to. This concept scheme is typically associated with the catalog using dcat:themeTaxonomy.

entries.need: Identify and describe a concept scheme.
entries.label: concept scheme
entries.definition: A knowledge organization system (KOS) used to represent themes/categories of datasets in the catalog.
